title: Spend tokens where they change the answer
summary: Estimate request cost, cache stable context, route work to the right model, and count cost per success.

scenario.briefing: The tutoring assistant sends the whole course outline and every prior message on each turn, always uses the largest model, and retries invalid output without a limit. The monthly bill tripled while answer quality stayed flat. Make the cost visible and choose where to spend.

objectives.description: Estimate token cost from usage and prices.
Identify avoidable spend in the request path.
Explain caching, routing, and cost per success.

hints: Cost is input tokens times input price plus output tokens times output price.
Prices are usually quoted per million tokens, so divide by one million.
Round money to a stable precision before comparing.
Measure cost per successful answer, including retries and cached input.

misconceptions.feedback: Output tokens usually cost more than input. A cost model that ignores them understates the bill.

misconceptions.description: Sending every request to the largest model.
misconceptions.feedback: Reserve the largest model for tasks that need it. Route simple extraction and formatting to a smaller model and keep a measured fallback.

misconceptions.description: Choosing the model with the lowest price per token regardless of failures.
misconceptions.feedback: A cheap model that fails validation and retries can cost more per success. Measure quality, retries, and latency together.

sections.title: Price the whole request
sections.body: Input and output tokens have separate prices, and cached input may be cheaper. Convert quoted per-million prices to the unit you report, and round consistently so small differences do not create false regressions.

sections.title: Cache what does not change
sections.body: A stable system prompt or policy pack can be cached across requests. Conversation history and per-user data change, so they cannot share a cache entry. Caching the wrong prefix either misses or leaks context.

sections.title: Optimize cost per success
sections.body: A cheap call that fails validation and retries twice may cost more than one larger call. Route by task difficulty, cap output, and track cost per accepted answer rather than cost per request.

steps.title: Estimate request cost
steps.prompt: Edit cost.js. estimateCost(inputTokens, outputTokens, inputPerMillion, outputPerMillion) returns the cost in dollars, rounded to six decimal places. Prices are dollars per one million tokens.
hints: Multiply each token count by its per-million price.
Divide the sum by one million.
Round only at the end, to six decimals.
Return 0 when both token counts are zero.

tests.description: Combines small input and output counts.
tests.name: estimateCost

steps.title: Find the avoidable spend
steps.prompt: Select every supported finding and choose a verdict.
hints: Look at which model every request uses.
Check what is resent on each turn.
Look for retry and output limits.
Change the path: route by task, cache stable context, and cap retries.

artifact.title: Tutoring request path
artifact.caption: Every turn uses the same model and resends the course pack.

findings.label: Every turn uses the largest model, including simple formatting and extraction.
The whole course pack and every prior message are resent on each turn.
The stable course pack is not cached.
A validation failure triggers another unbounded call with the same prompt.
Lowering temperature is the primary way to reduce token spend.

verdicts.label: Revise routing, context, cache, and retry limits
Only set a monthly budget alert

steps.explanation: Routing, context size, caching, and retry policy each change spend. A budget alert reports the problem after the money is spent.

steps.title: Spend on the task, not the habit
hints: Different tasks need different model capability.
A retry is part of the cost of a call.
Measure accepted answers, not raw requests.
Select routing, caching, output caps, and cost per success; reject cheapest-token thinking.

statements.label: Route simple extraction and formatting to a smaller, cheaper model when it passes the same evaluation.
Cache stable instructions and policy text, not per-user conversation history.
An output cap bounds the most expensive part of a request.
Cost per successful answer includes retries and failed validation.
The model with the lowest price per token always has the lowest cost per success.

steps.explanation: Routing, caching, output caps, and success-weighted measurement align spend with useful work.
